The app needs location permission to read your position once. It is only used to calculate prayer times and the Qibla direction, and it never leaves your phone. GPS works without internet, but the first fix can take a minute or two; go outdoors or near a window if it is slow.
Finding your location… This can take up to two minutes.
Location permission was not given. You can still search for a city or enter coordinates.
Location permission is turned off for this app. To use GPS, allow it in the app\'s system settings, or choose a city or coordinates instead.
Location is turned off on this phone. Turn it on in system settings, or choose a city or coordinates instead.
Your location could not be found. Try again outdoors, or choose a city or coordinates instead.
Use decimal degrees. South latitudes and west longitudes are negative, for example 51.5074 and -0.1278 for London.
Check the time zone is right for this place. It decides the clock time shown for each prayer.
Enter a decimal number, such as 51.5074 or -0.1278.

Prayer times cannot be calculated here for this date, because the sun does not rise or does not set. Please follow your local mosque\'s timetable.
Fajr 18°, Isha 17°. Widely used in Europe, the Far East and parts of America.
Fajr 19.5°, Isha 17.5°. Used in much of Africa and the Middle East.
Fajr 18°, Isha 18°. Used in Pakistan, Bangladesh, India and Afghanistan.
Fajr 18.5°, Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib. Used in Saudi Arabia. In Ramadan the official Isha is 120 minutes after Maghrib; this is not applied automatically.
Fajr 18.2°, Isha 18.2°. Used in the United Arab Emirates.
Fajr and Isha 18° with seasonal adjustments. Used by some communities in North America and the UK.
Fajr 15°, Isha 15°. Used by the Islamic Society of North America.
Fajr 18°, Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib. Used in Qatar.
Fajr 20°, Isha 18°. In our checks, Malaysia\'s official (JAKIM) Fajr was 10 minutes later than this method.
Fajr 18°, Isha 17°, with adjustments that approximate Turkey\'s official times.
Asr begins when an object\'s shadow equals its length.
Asr begins when the shadow is twice the object\'s length (later).
One-seventh of the night above 48° latitude; middle of the night elsewhere.
Fajr no earlier, and Isha no later, than the middle of the night.
Fajr no earlier than the last seventh of the night; Isha no later than the first seventh.
Limits based on the Fajr and Isha angles (angle ÷ 60 of the night).
No single method is right for every community. Choose the one your local mosque uses.

Far from the equator the sun may not go low enough for the usual Fajr and Isha angles, especially in summer. These rules set a limit. Where the sun does not rise or set at all, times cannot be calculated.
Per-prayer minute adjustments will be added to Settings in a later stage.
